out.text: Decision stands. Dublin's storm window closed at 15:00Z, the 16:30Z METAR shows 11 kt gusting 22 kt, and 11 DUB departures operated 15:30–17:30Z. EI-NSB had been AOG since 23 Jan 21:40Z with an engine-driven pump leak and no MEL relief, logged before the storm, so the storm did not cause this cancellation.

Decision stands. The tier-1 technical log records an external leak at the EDP case drain port on EI-NSB at DUB, logged 23JAN 21:40Z, exceeding the AMM limit with no MEL relief and the aircraft AOG, and the pool replacement unit had an ETA of 25JAN 14:00Z. The DUB storm window had closed at 15:00Z, the 241630Z METAR shows gusts of only 22KT, and 11 DUB departures operated 15:30–17:30Z, so NS31 was cancelled because of the technical fault, not the weather. The challenge brings nothing new to check, so no question has been routed and the engine's finding stands.

Decision stands. A manufacturer's notice of a hidden defect in the pump batch is a new legal question (CJEU C-549/07 ¶26), so it has gone to Legal, and the decision does not change unless Legal rules. On the evidence today EI-NSB was AOG from 23 Jan 21:40Z with no MEL relief, logged before Dublin's storm window closed at 15:00Z.

Decision stands. The tier-1 technical log shows EI-NSB grounded at DUB at 23JAN 21:40Z with an EDP case drain leak exceeding the AMM limit and no MEL relief, before the storm window opened, and the pool replacement unit had an ETA of 25JAN 14:00Z. The DUB storm window closed at 15:00Z, the EIDW 241630Z METAR read 23011G22KT, and 11 DUB departures operated 15:30–17:30Z. Your argument that this could be an extraordinary circumstance, such as a hidden manufacturing defect under CJEU C-549/07, has gone to Legal, and the decision does not change unless Legal rules, because the engine decides facts; Legal rules on law.

Dear {{passenger_name}},

We are writing about your booking {{booking_reference}}. Your flight NS108 on 24 January 2025 was cancelled. The cause was Storm Éowyn: departure inside Dublin's storm window. We are sorry for the disruption to your journey.

This notice sets out your rights under Regulation (EC) No 261/2004, as Article 14(2) of that Regulation requires.

For this cancellation there is no compensation; refunds and care still due. Under Article 5(3), no compensation is payable when a cancellation is caused by extraordinary circumstances that could not have been avoided even if all reasonable measures had been taken. This cancellation falls under that rule. The same article makes clear that your right to a refund or re-routing and your right to care remain in full.

Under Article 8, you may choose one of the following. You can have the price of your ticket reimbursed within seven days. Or you can be re-routed to your final destination at the earliest opportunity, or at a later date of your choosing. No refund has been started on this booking yet. Please contact us and quote your booking reference to tell us which option you want.

Under Article 9, you are entitled to care while you wait for your re-routed flight. This means meals and refreshments, hotel accommodation where necessary, and transport between the airport and the hotel. You may also make two telephone calls or send two emails. If you paid for any of these yourself, please send us your receipts with your booking reference so that we can review them.

If you are not satisfied with how we have handled your case, you can contact the national enforcement body at {{neb_contact}}.

Yours sincerely,

Northstar Air Customer Care

If you need help, you can contact the national enforcement body: {{neb_contact}}.

Dear {{passenger_name}},

This notice is about your booking {{booking_reference}} on Northstar Air flight NS31 on 24 January 2025, which was cancelled. Article 14(2) of Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 requires us to set out your rights in writing.

We previously sent you a message that was wrong. It said: "Your flight NS31 on 24 Jan was cancelled due to weather (extraordinary circumstances). No compensation is payable under EU261." That is not correct. The cancellation was caused by a technical fault on the aircraft (engine-driven pump leak logged before the storm), not the weather. Compensation is therefore owed to you. We apologise for the error.

You are entitled to compensation of €600. Under Article 7(3), we pay compensation in cash, by bank transfer or by cheque. We can pay it in travel vouchers only if you agree to this in writing and sign that agreement.

Under Article 8, you have the right to a refund of your ticket or to re-routing to your final destination. A refund for your booking has already been initiated. It will not be repeated.

Under Article 9, you are also entitled to care. This includes meals and refreshments, hotel accommodation where necessary, transport between the airport and the hotel, and telephone calls or emails. If you paid for any of these yourself because of the cancellation, please contact us with your receipts and your booking reference {{booking_reference}}.

If you are not satisfied with how we handle your claim, you may contact the national enforcement body: {{neb_contact}}

Yours sincerely,

Northstar Air Customer Care
